items.answer: There is one requirement delivered as one card, so there is nothing to order. All of it is Must.

Module src/ratings/notch.mjs. (a) RATING_SCALE is an ordered list of the 19 canonical upper-case symbols, best first: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-. (b) notchChange(previous: string, current: string) returns an integer equal to index(current) - index(previous) on that scale. It is synchronous. Downgrade is positive, upgrade negative, unchanged 0. Unit: notches (one scale step). Range: -18 (CCC- → AAA) to +18 (AAA → CCC-). Inputs are normalised with String.prototype.trim() and matched case-insensitively. There is no null/empty handling other than rejection (C2).
items.quote: `RATING_SCALE` — the 19 ratings of C1, best first. … `notchChange(previous, current)` → integer (C3). … Rating scale, best to worst (19 steps): AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-.

items.answer: Any invalid argument (previous or current) throws a RangeError. This is a RangeError, not a TypeError, even for non-strings. Invalid means: (1) a non-string, such as undefined, null, a number, an object, or a String object like new String('A'); (2) an empty string, or a string that is empty after trim(), such as '   '; (3) a string that after trim() and case-folding is not one of the 19 C1 ratings, such as 'CC', 'C', 'D', 'NR', 'Baa1', 'BBB +', 'AAA+'. There is no fallback value and no partial result.
